tone_statements.citation: Kuang, Jianjing. 2013. The tonal space of contrastive five level tones. Phonetica 70(1-2): 1-23. doi:10.1159/000353853.
tone_statements.quote: According to Li’s transcription, there are eight tones (I–VIII) in this dialect; five of them are level tones, two rising and one falling (using Chao’s tonal representation), as shown in table 2. Tone VIII (11), tone IV (22), tone VI (33), tone I (44), and tone III (55) are the five levels. There is no ‘neutral’ tone as found in some Sinitic languages. ... We confirmed that pitch is not the only cue for tonal contrasts in this language, and non-modal phonations appear to be very important cues in both tonal production and perception.
tone_statements.locator: p. 5, sec. 2 'Black Miao' (with Table 2, p. 6); second sentence p. 17, sec. 6
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: Eight tones (44 51 55 22 45 33 13 11), five of them level; F0 production (8 male speakers) and AX perception show breathy/laryngealized phonation helps separate 11, 33, 55; 22 vs 44 most confusable.

sources.citation: Liu, Wen, You-Jing Lin, Zhenghui Yang & Jiangping Kong. 2020 [online 4 Dec 2018]. Hmu (Xinzhai variety). Journal of the International Phonetic Association 50(2): 240-257. doi:10.1017/S0025100318000336 (open access).
sources.note: No stress/prosody paragraph at all. Sections: Consonants, Vowels, Tones (8 tones incl. five level tones; breathy voice on /11/; 'tone sandhi is not observed in Hmu'), Syllable structure ('obligatory nucleus (V) on a specific tone'; 'phonologically monosyllabic with a strong tendency towards disyllabicity in its lexicon. Multi-syllabic words are mostly compounds'). Word 'stress' occurs only in a cited reference title.
sources.venue: Journal of the International Phonetic Association

sources.citation: Ratliff, Martha. 2010. Hmong-Mien language history. Pacific Linguistics 613. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics.
sources.note: Family-level only: p.199 (sec. 4.2.1) Hmong-Mien nominal prefixes 'are unstressed, and in some languages they may harmonize with the nouns to which they are attached (Chen 1993)'; p.28 quotes Downer on iambic rhythm in Mien (not Hmongic). Nothing specific to Hmu word stress.

sources.citation: Kuang, Jianjing. 2013. Phonation in tonal contrasts. PhD dissertation, UCLA (ch. 4: Black Miao = Qingjiang Miao of Shidongkou, Taijiang county).
sources.note: Nothing on word stress; instrumental study of the 8 tones (44 51 55 22 45 33 13 11) and phonation on isolated monosyllables; notes the site is Li Fang-kuei's 1940s Black Miao village and that Kwan 1966 partially reports Li's transcriptions.

sources.citation: Wang Fushi 王辅世 (主编). 1985. 苗语简志 Miaoyu jianzhi [A sketch of the Miao language]. 中国少数民族语言简志丛书. Beijing: 民族出版社. 2+203 pp. (Yanghao 养蒿, Kaili = representative of Qiandong/Northern Hmu, pp. 13-16; general remarks p. 3)
sources.note: Nothing for Yanghao/Hmu. p.3: every syllable has a tone that distinguishes meaning; Yanghao section (pp.13-16) gives initials, rhymes, 8 tones (33 55 35 11 44 13 53 31), allophony; no 重音/轻声/轻读 remark for Yanghao (the book's only 轻声 remark, p.12, is about Layiping = Western Xong prefixes qo35/ta35/te35). Ch'ien-tung (Qiandong) is said to lack tone sandhi.
sources.venue: 中国少数民族语言简志丛书

sources.citation: Liu, Wen, Gang Peng & Jiangping Kong. 2024. The role of breathy voice in Hmu tone perception. Journal of Chinese Linguistics 52(1): 138-174. doi:10.1353/jcl.2024.a919401 (preprint version 2023, doi:10.1353/jcl.2017.a912223).
sources.tag: likely states tone; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: online with restricted access (login, paywall or limited view)
sources.note: Crossref abstract (seen): 'This study investigates the role of non-modal phonation in perceiving the five level tones used in Hmu, in which the lowest level tone (T11) is often referred to as "breathy voice". First, an acoustic analysis was conducted on those tones to determine the voice quality.. revealing that breathiness only co-occurs with T11. Second, a perception experiment.. Results show that identification scores significantly differ only for the pairs of two continua that involve T11.. native speakers rely on breathiness in T11 identification.' Unpaywall: closed; MUSE landing behind…

tone.summary: Hmu five level tones (11-55) within the 8-tone system; breathy phonation co-occurs only with T11 and is used perceptually (from abstract).
